title: ICE Emails Discuss Using Palantir-Supported Tool to Investigate Voter Fraud
gist: FOIA documents published by Democracy Forward show ICE's Homeland Security Investigations, via its iLab, discussed ingesting processed voter roll data into ELITE, a Palantir-supported enforcement targeting system, as part of voter-fraud investigations ahead of the midterms; Palantir says voter roll data has never been integrated into ELITE. DHS has investigated 150+ nonprofits but found only a handful of possible noncitizen voting cases.

themes.theme: ICE repurposing enforcement tech for voter fraud

insights.claim: A May 26 HSI email says iLab's processing focuses on DOJ voting rolls and USCIS data, with criminal histories currently excluded but efforts underway to add them.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Shows federal data-fusion efforts expanding into election data, a policy and contractor-risk issue.
insights.quote: “iLab’s processing focuses on DOJ voting rolls and [US Citizenship and Immigration Services] data; criminal histories are currently excluded, with efforts underway to address this,”

insights.claim: HSI staff discussed ingesting processed voter roll data into the ELITE enforcement system to enhance lead management, analytical review and investigative tracking.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Potential expansion of Palantir-supported tools into election enforcement raises political and reputational risk for Palantir.
insights.quote: particularly on ingesting processed voter roll data into the ELITE enforcement system to enhance lead management, analytical review, and investigative tracking.

insights.claim: A July 7 DHS 'Fraud WAR' email said data for Connecticut, Georgia, Kentucky, Missouri, Michigan and New Mexico had been enriched by iLab and were pending Palantir entry into ELITE, with the update to be sent to the White House.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Ties Palantir's government platform directly to a politically charged White House-watched initiative.

insights.claim: Palantir says voter roll data has never been integrated into ELITE, and ICE declines to disclose investigative methods.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Palantir is distancing itself from election use, signaling sensitivity to reputational blowback.
insights.quote: “Voter roll data has never been integrated into ELITE,” a Palantir spokesman tells WIRED.

insights.claim: ELITE (Enhanced Leads Identification & Targeting for Enforcement), first reported by 404 Media, lets ICE agents map potential deportation targets, pull files on each and see a 'confidence score' on a person's current address.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Describes the capability set of a key Palantir-supported government product.

insights.claim: Fordham's Chinmayi Sharma believes ICE is building the voter-fraud system for the future rather than deploying it now, and that DHS is used because of its existing authorities, infrastructure, vendor relationships and contract vehicles.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Existing enforcement contract vehicles make it easy to extend vendor platforms like Palantir's into new mission areas, expanding TAM but also controversy.
insights.quote: I think it's because of the authorities, the infrastructure, the vendor relationships, the contract vehicles, and privileges. There's just a lot of synergies you can take advantage of.

insights.claim: Sharma says ICE wants a system that learns to find people to investigate and potentially bring action against, building on existing infrastructure and data sources.

insights.so_what: Gap between rhetoric and evidence signals the effort is political, heightening litigation and backlash risk.
